what: tempo: 27 "no `assert` in `crate`" in the antithesis members. antithesis_sdk's assert_sometimes! writes a block whose `#[$crate::linkme::distributed_slice($crate::assert::ANTITHESIS_CATALOG)] static ..` is a statement; the names stage reads the statements as items (statements_as_items) and a macro-written body's block as a module (make_blocks), both texts COPIED from the expansion, and a call in them took its input as that text lexed again, where another crate's `$crate` is the plain keyword `crate`. linkme's output `crate::assert::ANTITHESIS_CATALOG! {..}` was then looked for in the calling crate.
cost: about two hours; the first fixture shapes (item-level `$p:path`, `$t:tt`, `$e:expr`) passed on the old tree, the bug needs a statement call or a macro-written body
cause: a rewritten text carried no tokens of the expansion it was copied from, so its calls fell back to lexing text
whys: token marks live on ExpansionTokens; the two rewrites report the slices they copy (Copied) for marks, but nothing moved the tokens with them
class: a text rewritten from an expansion that keeps the marks' map but not the tokens: any `$crate` (or other hygiene context) of a call inside it is lost
prevention: done: ExpansionTokens::moved places the expansion's tokens by the same Copied list; both rewrites and a block's body pass them on; test crates/blaze-cli/tests/check_dollar_crate_through_an_argument.rs
annoyance: the runner keeps only cargo's ---- stdout ---- blocks, so `-- --nocapture` hides a failing test's words; the names stage does not report an unresolved path in a const's TYPE (`const _: $crate::m::Y = ..` says nothing), so the first control could not fail
workaround: run without --nocapture; the control is a macro path instead
